vizqueryearth.title: Regional Ocean Modeling Interviews
vizqueryearth.description: These rules were extracted by Claude from five expert interviews on regional ocean modeling (https://aidanjanney.github.io/RegionalOceanModelingInterviews/), and no expert has reviewed them; each rule quotes the passages it rests on. Draw your domain and give your grid resolution in km to see which rules apply.

properties.name: REGION/CORALTRIANGLE/CORALTRIANGLE001
properties.title: Coral Triangle tidal mixing is missing without tides
properties.message: The Coral Triangle has many small, shallow, interconnected basins and narrow straits where intense tidal mixing plays a dominant role, amplified in the narrow passages by local resonance. Models without tidal forcing under-represent this mixing; global models commonly compensate by raising local mixing artificially.
properties.instruction: Include tidal forcing, or, if the model runs without tides, raise mixing in the narrow passages to stand in for tidal mixing.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: the region consists of many small, shallow, and interconnected basins with narrow straits, where intense tidal mixing plays a dominant role
Global models often lack tidal forcing, so they under-represent the mixing
it’s common to increase local mixing artificially in these models

properties.name: REGION/CORALTRIANGLE/CORALTRIANGLE002
properties.title: Validate Coral Triangle tides against tide gauges
properties.message: There are enough tide gauges in the region to validate tidal phase and amplitude. The tides are complex: some areas are semidiurnal, others diurnal and many mixed, and getting all of that right is a key challenge.
properties.instruction: Compare modeled tidal amplitude and phase with tide gauges across the diurnal, semidiurnal and mixed areas.

properties.name: REGION/CORALTRIANGLE/CORALTRIANGLE003
properties.title: Torres Strait: near-zero mean flow, easily exaggerated
properties.message: The strait between Australia and Papua New Guinea is extremely shallow, with near-zero net transport on average. On a coarse grid a single cell that is too wide or too deep exaggerates its transport, which is why many global models close it. At higher resolution it can be left open, and the model can then resolve the tidal reversals that dominate the instantaneous flow while keeping a near-zero mean.
properties.instruction: On a coarse grid, check this strait's transport and consider closing it; at higher resolution, leave it open and check that its mean transport stays near zero.

evidence.quote: It’s extremely shallow, with a near-zero net transport on average

properties.name: REGION/CORALTRIANGLE/CORALTRIANGLE004
properties.title: Gather in situ data and work with local scientists
properties.message: Satellite data are tricky in the Coral Triangle: the topography is complex and the signal can be noisy or unreliable. Start by assembling buoy records, tide gauge data and other in situ measurements as a baseline, and work with scientists in the region who have in situ observations and local knowledge, which the expert called good practice and more ethical.
properties.instruction: Assemble buoy, tide gauge and other in situ records, and collaborate with researchers working in the region.

properties.name: REGION/CORALTRIANGLE/CORALTRIANGLE005
properties.title: Represent river inflow from rainy small islands
properties.message: River freshwater input is often simplified in small island systems. Islands in regions like the Coral Triangle have no large drainage basins but receive substantial rainfall, and better river inflows, especially in the monsoon season, can change coastal salinity and nutrient delivery; they may matter more than previously assumed.
properties.instruction: Include river inflows from the islands, with their monsoon-season variation, rather than simplifying them away.

evidence.quote: Freshwater input from rivers is one area that often gets simplified, particularly in small island systems
Improved representation of river inflows—especially during the monsoon season—can influence coastal salinity and nutrient delivery, and might be more important than previously assumed

properties.name: REGION/CORALTRIANGLE/CORALTRIANGLE006
properties.title: Include benthic carbonate fluxes over reefs
properties.message: Once biogeochemistry is added, benthic fluxes over shelves and reefs, often overlooked in global models, are crucial for accuracy in regions like the Coral Triangle, where calcium carbonate production and dissolution can shift local carbonate chemistry significantly. Field programs in the region sometimes deploy moored buoys that record alkalinity and dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), which can show whether the simulated carbonate system is realistic.
properties.instruction: Represent benthic exchanges over reefs and shelves, and compare the carbonate system with buoy alkalinity and DIC time series.

evidence.quote: These benthic exchanges have often been overlooked in global models, but they're crucial for accuracy in regions like the Coral Triangle

properties.name: REGION/ITF/ITF001
properties.title: Benchmark Indonesian Throughflow transport
properties.message: Transport through the Indonesian Throughflow, which carries water and heat from the Pacific to the Indian Ocean, is a critical evaluation metric. The flow branches across several passages, and observational campaigns have given transport estimates for key straits. Check how much water gets through and how well its structure and timing are captured, against observational estimates, reanalysis and in situ data such as moored arrays.
properties.instruction: Compare modeled transport through each main strait, and its structure and timing, with observational estimates.

Transports across chokepoints—like the Indonesian Throughflow or Agulhas leakage—would also be important
All of that should be benchmarked against reanalysis, satellite observations, and any in situ data that are available, including Argo floats or moored arrays
It plays a big role in global climate dynamics by transporting water and heat from the Pacific to the Indian Ocean

properties.name: REGION/ITF/ITF002
properties.title: Fix the ITF strait split with bathymetry, not viscosity
properties.message: Tuning viscosity early was not enough to get the relative transport through each strait right; the main adjustment was to the bathymetry, and reaching realistic transports took multiple iterations, potentially 20 or more. In coarse global models the passages can be a single grid cell wide; in a finer regional model, check that the narrow straits are actually resolved.
properties.instruction: If the transport split between straits is wrong, revise the strait bathymetry rather than relying on viscosity alone, and expect many iterations.

properties.name: REGION/ITF/ITF003
properties.title: Lombok Strait spans only a few cells even at 5 km
properties.message: Lombok Strait is thousands of meters deep on either side but narrows to about 200 m in the middle, so even at 5 km resolution it may span only a few grid cells. The steep vertical and horizontal gradients make its transport hard to resolve, especially with sigma coordinates, which are sensitive to abrupt topography.
properties.instruction: Check how the grid represents Lombok Strait's sill depth and width before trusting its transport.

properties.name: REGION/INDIAN/INDIAN001
properties.title: Indian Ocean: extend the domain from Africa to Australia
properties.message: For an Indian Ocean model, the expert's ideal domain extends from the east coast of Africa across to Western Australia, to minimize problematic open boundaries. Rather than placing a boundary around the Mozambique Channel or near Indonesia, include the whole region so key pathways such as the Indonesian Throughflow are not truncated. The wider domain costs more to run, but the payoff is fewer errors from artificial boundaries.
properties.instruction: Avoid open boundaries in the Mozambique Channel or near Indonesia; extend the domain to the coasts instead.

properties.name: REGION/INDIAN/INDIAN002
properties.title: Check the Somali Current's seasonal reversal
properties.message: Seasonally reversing monsoon winds drive Indian Ocean western boundary currents such as the Somali Current. The key question is whether the model captures the seasonal reversal in both magnitude and timing.
properties.instruction: Check that the modeled Somali Current reverses with the monsoon with the right magnitude and timing.

properties.name: REGION/INDIAN/INDIAN003
properties.title: Check Arabian and Western Australian upwelling
properties.message: Upwelling zones such as those near the Arabian Peninsula and off Western Australia should show clearly in SST and are good early targets for spotting anything drastically off. Check whether their surface temperatures are cool enough and whether the thermocline shoals in the right places. The broad features will most likely look roughly right at first glance, so quantify their magnitude and extent.
properties.instruction: Quantify the magnitude and extent of these upwelling zones from SST and thermocline depth.

properties.name: REGION/BENGUELA/BENGUELA001
properties.title: Benguela warm SST biases persist at high resolution
properties.message: The Benguela stands out as a system where substantial biases, such as a warm SST bias, remain even at finer resolution. Local causes include insufficient resolution in the coastal wind forcing, which can weaken coastal jets and reduce upwelling; remote causes include tropical Atlantic SST biases that may teleconnect into the region. A regional model lets you experiment with the boundary conditions to separate how much of the bias comes from outside and how much is local.
properties.instruction: Use well-resolved coastal wind forcing, and test the boundary conditions to separate remote from local sources of bias.

properties.name: REGION/BENGUELA/BENGUELA002
properties.title: The Angola–Benguela Front is tied to bathymetry
properties.message: The sharp front between the warm southward flow and the cold Benguela Current is strongly controlled by the underlying topography, and studies tie the location of the frontal zone near 16°S to bathymetric features. Getting the bathymetry and coastline right is important; once the resolution is high enough to represent them, the expert would not expect much tuning of physics parameters to be needed.
properties.instruction: Check the bathymetry and coastline near the front before tuning physics parameters.

properties.name: REGION/BENGUELA/BENGUELA003
properties.title: Benguela domain: north edge near 7°S, west to 0°E
properties.message: To separate remote from local drivers, include the Benguela upwelling zone and parts of the Angola coast, but do not extend too far north into the tropical Atlantic, where the flow becomes zonal and would enter obliquely through the northern boundary; the expert suggested perhaps around 7°S. Extend slightly west of the Cape of Good Hope to capture the Agulhas retroflection, out to at least 0°E or a bit farther if the retroflection is part of the focus, so that no boundary cuts through the Agulhas Return Current or the frontal zone.
properties.instruction: Consider a northern boundary around 7°S and, if the Agulhas retroflection is in scope, a western boundary at or west of 0°E.

properties.name: REGION/BENGUELA/BENGUELA004
properties.title: Get the Benguela mean state right before probing drivers
properties.message: Before studying remote versus local drivers, check the basic mean state: the large-scale currents, the frontal position and the SST, especially the upwelling signature. Avoiding the warm bias seen in global models is a good sign. Then perturb forcings, such as the northern boundary inflow or the surface wind stress, rather than internal physics like mixing schemes or viscosity, at least as a first step, and see what disrupts the solution.
properties.instruction: Validate currents, front position and upwelling SST first; then vary boundary inflow and wind forcing before touching mixing or viscosity.

properties.title: Keep the North Brazil retroflection inside the domain
properties.message: Placing a boundary right at a retroflection usually leads to trouble. Off the north coast of Brazil there is a retroflection associated with eddy shedding; even though it is a strong current region, it is better to include it than to end the domain in a messy, energetic area.
properties.instruction: Extend the domain to include the retroflection rather than placing a boundary in it.

properties.name: REGION/NWA/NWA001
properties.title: Check for a coherent deep western boundary current
properties.message: In the Northwest Atlantic the Gulf Stream can be particularly challenging, and SST patterns may show problems without explaining their causes. One early diagnostic is whether the model produces a realistic, coherent deep western boundary current, judged from subsurface currents; observations at depth are limited, but the check is still worth doing.

properties.name: REGION/NWA/NWA002
properties.title: Test bathymetry choices at Cape Hatteras and the slopes
properties.message: Try a few methods of generating the bathymetry to see whether they change key circulation features; often they do not have a major impact, but the tests show whether bathymetry limits the model's accuracy. Look especially at Cape Hatteras, where the Gulf Stream leaves the shelf, and at the steep continental slopes off the northeastern and southeastern U.S., where wide shelves drop off sharply and the topography can affect current separation and path.

properties.name: REGION/NWA/NWA003
properties.title: Horizontal viscosity is a first lever on the Gulf Stream
properties.message: Horizontal viscosity consistently plays a role in Gulf Stream simulations: adjusting it can significantly change the current's path, strength and mean position, and it is often one of the first tuning levers. It involves trade-offs, since a more accurate path can come with a current that is too weak or too strong elsewhere. In most regional work this tuning is done by hand, through trial and error.
properties.instruction: Use horizontal viscosity as an early lever on the Gulf Stream path, and check current strength elsewhere for side effects.

references.title: Expert interview 3: Northwest Atlantic Seasonal Forecasting

properties.name: REGION/NWA/NWA004
properties.title: Favor Gulf Stream separation or Florida Current by goal
properties.message: The Gulf Stream's separation point is sensitive to the strength of the western boundary current through the Florida Straits, so a viscosity that is not physically optimal may be needed to make it separate at a realistic latitude. For temperature, salinity or ecosystem studies in the northeast U.S., the separation location matters far more than the current strength near Florida; for western boundary transport or the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, the Florida Current strength matters more.
properties.instruction: Decide from the study's goal whether to favor a realistic separation latitude or a realistic Florida Current strength when tuning viscosity.

properties.name: SETUP/BGC/BGC002
properties.title: Satellite chlorophyll is uncertain, especially near land
properties.message: Many biogeochemical observations come from satellite products, and satellite chlorophyll in particular is highly uncertain: it is derived from subtle optical signals that are sensitive to retrieval algorithms, organic content and water clarity, and proximity to land can contaminate it, which matters for shallow coral reef systems that are often near land. A model can have plausible physical and biogeochemical processes and still differ noticeably from satellite estimates, so a one-to-one match should not be expected.
properties.instruction: Expect some divergence from satellite chlorophyll, and check products for land contamination before using them in coastal or reef areas.
